source.title: A randomized proof-of-mechanism trial applying the 'fast-fail' approach to evaluating kappa-opioid antagonism as a treatment for anhedonia

confidence_rationale: High-quality multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT (n=89) with a pre-registered fMRI primary endpoint: a selective KOR antagonist (JNJ-67953964) significantly increased ventral-striatum activation during reward anticipation in patients with anhedonia and a mood/anxiety disorder. This is the human proof-of-mechanism the layer's kappa-axis proposal and PHARM-018 falsification condition turn on. Confidence below 0.8 because the primary endpoint is a circuit biomarker (reward-anticipation activation), not a clinical anhedonia or commitment endpoint, and it does not isolate a 'commitment-entropy' construct from general reward-circuit engagement.
failure_signatures: The trial demonstrates target engagement on a reward-anticipation circuit biomarker, not clinical anhedonia remission or any commitment/perseveration measure; a positive biomarker does not establish that the kappa axis is dissociable from the serotonin axis on clinical endpoints (the PHARM-018 falsification still stands open).

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a NIMH fast-fail proof-of-mechanism RCT (selective KOR antagonist JNJ-67953964 10 mg, n=45, vs placebo n=44) in patients with anhedonia and a mood or anxiety disorder, the KOR antagonist significantly increased fMRI ventral-striatum activation during reward anticipation relative to placebo (effect size 0.58), with good tolerability.
mapping.ree_translation: The layer proposes a kappa-driven commitment-entropy vulnerability axis (a candidate amendment to ARC-086) distinct from the serotonin-terrain and dopamine-selection axes, with PHARM-018 predicting that kappa antagonism normalises pathological aversive-state-lock / anhedonia via the kappa-antagonist arm. Krystal et al. provide the human target-engagement proof: blocking KOR demonstrably re-engages the reward-anticipation circuitry whose hypofunction REE reads as the aversive-attractor-dominant state.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The endpoint is a reward-anticipation CIRCUIT BIOMARKER (ventral-striatum fMRI), not clinical anhedonia remission and certainly not a commitment/perseveration measure. It establishes that kappa antagonism engages reward circuitry in humans; it does NOT establish dissociation from the serotonin axis on clinical endpoints, nor validate the commitment-entropy construct -- the PHARM-018 falsification condition remains open.
mapping.source_context: Human; multicentre double-blind placebo-controlled RCT; fMRI reward-anticipation primary endpoint; anhedonia with mood/anxiety disorder.

confidence_components.notes: Top-tier human RCT with pre-registered biomarker endpoint; transfer risk low (human anhedonia). Mapping_fidelity moderate-good for 'kappa antagonism engages human reward circuitry'; the limiter is biomarker-vs-clinical-endpoint and the unvalidated commitment-entropy construct.
